A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TabReD benchmark. All 31 pages, including Appendices A–E, are readable and aligned. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish that differences are confined to the version stamp and one bibliographic entry.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations on eight TabReD datasets (Table 2), temporal-versus-random split experiments (Figure 1), and an audit of existing datasets (Table 1 and Appendix E).

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark evaluations, split-comparison experiments, and dataset audit reported in Tables 1–2, Figure 1, and Appendix E.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction and method adaptations are unchanged, including causal TabR retrieval, temporal domains for CORAL, and DFR fine-tuning in Section 4 and Appendix B.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight TabReD datasets, covering three classification and five regression tasks, and the same temporal-versus-random evaluation scenarios. The existing-dataset audit is also unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the identical classical ML, deep learning, and OOD comparator sets. Section 4.2 retains MLP, MLP-PLR, XGBoost, and TabR-S for the split comparison.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain the same preprocessing, subsampling, metrics, training, and tuning protocols. Section 4.2 still compares three temporal splits with three corresponding random splits of matching sizes.

E4.justification: The temporal-split analysis, causal retrieval comparison, and OOD robustness evaluations are unchanged. Appendix E retains the same dataset-quality and leakage analyses.

E5.justification: Both report 15 random initializations, the same standard-deviation-based comparison and ranking procedure, and averaging across three splits in Section 4.2. Uncertainty reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–2, plotted results in Figure 1, and reported qualitative findings match. The appendix dataset statistics and annotations are also identical.

T1.justification: The mathematical ranking rule in Appendix B.2 is unchanged. Neither version contains a theorem or proof contribution, and no mathematical definitions or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about representative industrial datasets, temporal splits affecting model rankings, and the effectiveness of GBDTs and MLPs with numerical embeddings.

C2.justification: The interpretations of temporal shift, possible time-based leakage, and retrieval-model difficulties are unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning domain coverage, industrial bias, and unavailable feature descriptions.

D1.justification: The implementation details, preprocessing instructions, tuning budgets, dataset statistics, and code/data access information are unchanged throughout the main text and Appendices A–D. PDF link targets also match.

R1.justification: Reference [34] remains the same Kohli et al. work; v3 adds its ICLR 2024 Data-centric Machine Learning Research Workshop venue. This is bibliographic metadata completion, with no added cited work or changed research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 updates the arXiv version/date stamp and adds publication-venue metadata to reference [34]. The scientific prose, terminology, headings, and document structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added venue locally changes line wrapping and italicized text within reference [34] on page 11. Tables 1–2, Figure 1, appendix displays, and their placement are otherwise identical.

improvement.justification: v3 completes the venue information for one existing reference and updates the version stamp. The scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility information—including all appendices—are unchanged. The small bibliographic refinement does not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
